Core Acceptance Reference  Web: representative journeys pass WCAG 2.2 AA automated checks plus manual keyboard, focus, zoom, reflow, screen reader, and human accessibility review.  Documents: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF outputs preserve headings, reading order, tables, links, language metadata, alt text, contrast, and keyboard or screen reader usability.  Media: captions are accurate, synchronized, readable, and identify meaningful speakers and sounds; audio description is supplied when important visual information is otherwise unavailable.  Localization: no hard-coded or untranslated strings, broken placeholders, truncation, glyph loss, date or number errors, bidirectional defects, or locale fallback failures.  Filipino and English: terminology, grammar, tone, cultural context, Philippine formats, and accessibility language receive qualified bilingual human review.  Human validation: disabled users and target-language reviewers test representative high-risk journeys before release, with accommodations and privacy protections.  Evidence: every failure records the artifact, environment, assistive technology or locale, repeatable steps, applicable rule, severity, remediation owner, and retest result. Catalog Design Notes  Keep each Skill narrowly scoped. Let a coordinating Skill assemble only the checks required for the artifact, platform, audience, and locale.  Use automation for breadth and repeatability, then use manual and human testing for behavior, comprehension, natural language, and real assistive-technology outcomes.  Pin browser, operating system, assistive technology, locale data, font, translation memory, termbase, and rule-set versions in every reproducible test.  Treat Filipino, Tagalog, Philippine English, and regional Philippine languages as explicit language or locale decisions rather than interchangeable labels.  Never claim conformance from an automated score alone. Preserve unresolved exceptions and the conditions under which each result was observed.
